::: {.tldr}
This handbook is a Quarto site stored in a GitHub repository. Every change is
a pull request. You don't need to install anything — GitHub's web editor lets
you fix typos and add small pages from your browser. Larger changes are
easier with a local Quarto install.
:::

## The simplest contribution: fixing a typo

1. On any handbook page, click **Edit this page** in the right margin.
2. GitHub opens the source `.qmd` file in its web editor.
3. Make your change. Click **Commit changes**.
4. GitHub will offer to open a pull request — accept the default.
5. The Managing Editor reviews and merges, usually within two business days.

That's it. You did not install anything.

## Adding a new page

1. Decide which section the page belongs to.
2. In GitHub's web UI, click **Add file → Create new file** in the relevant
   folder. Name it with kebab-case ending in `.qmd`, e.g.
   `cryptomator-setup.qmd`.
3. Copy the contents of [`templates/_page-template.qmd`](https://github.com/hks-epod/inclusion-economics-handbook/blob/main/templates/_page-template.qmd)
   as your starting point.
4. Fill in the frontmatter — at minimum: `title`, `status: draft`,
   `last-reviewed`, `owner-role`, and `hubs`.
5. Add a link to the new page in `_quarto.yml` under the relevant `sidebar`
   section.
6. Commit. GitHub Actions will build a preview within 2 minutes.
7. Open a pull request, tag `@hks-epod/handbook-editors`.

## Working locally (recommended for larger changes)

```bash
# One-time setup
brew install quarto                                # macOS; see quarto.org for others
git clone https://github.com/hks-epod/inclusion-economics-handbook.git
cd inclusion-economics-handbook

# Each session
git checkout -b your-branch-name
quarto preview                                     # live-reloading local server

# When done
git add .
git commit -m "Describe the change"
git push -u origin your-branch-name
# Then open a pull request on GitHub
```

## Style guide

- **Voice.** Direct, concrete, second-person. "You'll need to…" not "Researchers should…"
- **Length.** Aim for the shortest page that fully answers the question. If a
  page exceeds ~1,500 words, consider splitting.
- **Lists vs. prose.** Use lists only for list-shaped content. Default to prose.
- **Acronyms.** Spell out on first use, even common ones (PAP, MoU, DUA).
  Add to the [glossary](glossary.qmd) if it's not there yet.
- **Hub-specific content.** Use the `panel-tabset` pattern (see the
  [page template](https://github.com/hks-epod/inclusion-economics-handbook/blob/main/templates/_page-template.qmd))
  rather than creating three separate pages.

## Review and merge

- Typos, formatting fixes, link corrections: any handbook editor can merge.
- Substantive content changes: routed to the section's `owner-role` for review.
- New top-level sections or major restructuring: Director of Research Operations.

The CODEOWNERS file in the repo controls automatic review assignment.

Handbook Managing Editor — see the `#handbook` Slack channel.
